explain: RSiCl₃ has three hydrolysable Cl, so it gives a cross-linked network.

prompt: SiO₂ is a high-melting solid but CO₂ is a gas because SiO₂
explain: Si does not form stable pπ–pπ bonds; SiO₂ is a network of SiO₄ tetrahedra, while CO₂ is discrete O=C=O.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: [SiF₆]²⁻ exists but [CCl₆]²⁻ does not, because carbon
explain: The C valence shell (n = 2) has no d orbitals, so its covalency is limited to 4.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Ultra-pure silicon for semiconductors is obtained by
explain: Crude Si is first converted to SiCl₄ and reduced to Si; zone refining then gives ultra-pure Si.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Order of basic strength of Group 15 hydrides.
explain: Down the group, size increases and lone-pair availability decreases, so basicity falls.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which hydride of Group 15 is the strongest reducing agent?
explain: Reducing character increases down the group as M–H bond strength falls; BiH₃ is strongest.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which oxide of nitrogen is paramagnetic and colourless gas?
explain: NO has one unpaired electron (odd electron), colourless gas, paramagnetic; N₂O is diamagnetic.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Nature of N₂O, NO, NO₂ and N₂O₅ respectively.
explain: N₂O and NO are neutral oxides; NO₂ and N₂O₅ are acidic.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which Group 15 hydride has the smallest H–M–H bond angle?
explain: Bond angle falls down the group: NH₃ 107°, PH₃ 93.5°, AsH₃ 91.8°, SbH₃ 91.3°.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Group 16: hydrides, oxides, O vs S
prompt: Among H₂O, H₂S, H₂Se, H₂Te, which is the strongest reducing agent?
explain: Reducing power increases down the group as the H–E bond weakens; H₂Te is the strongest.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Group 16: hydrides, oxides, O vs S
prompt: Nature of the oxide SO₂ when dissolved in water
explain: SO₂ is an acidic oxide and forms sulphurous acid in water.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Cold dilute NaOH reacts with Cl₂ to give NaCl and which other product?
explain: Cold dilute: Cl₂ + 2NaOH → NaCl + NaOCl + H₂O; hot concentrated gives NaClO₃.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Hydrogen halide with the highest acidic strength in aqueous solution is:
explain: Weaker H–X bond down the group makes HI the strongest acid: HF < HCl < HBr < HI.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Group 18: noble gas properties & Xe compounds
prompt: Shape of XeO₃ molecule is:
explain: XeO₃: 3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair on Xe (sp³) gives a pyramidal shape.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Group 18: noble gas properties & Xe compounds
prompt: Shape of XeOF₄ is:
explain: XeOF₄: 5 bond pairs + 1 lone pair, sp³d², giving a square pyramidal shape.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Group 18: noble gas properties & Xe compounds
prompt: Hydrolysis of XeF₆ completely gives:
explain: Complete hydrolysis of XeF₆ gives XeO₃ and HF with no change in oxidation state (+6).

subject: Chemistry
topic: Group 18: noble gas properties & Xe compounds
prompt: Xenon fluorides XeF₂, XeF₄, XeF₆ are best prepared by direct reaction of Xe and F₂ under:
options: Presence of Pt at room temperature
explain: Xe + F₂ gives XeF₂, XeF₄ or XeF₆ depending on the Xe:F₂ ratio, temperature and pressure.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Group 18: noble gas properties & Xe compounds
prompt: XeF₆ reacts with silica (SiO₂) to give:
explain: 2XeF₆ + SiO₂ → 2XeOF₄ + SiF₄, so XeF₆ cannot be stored in glass or quartz.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acidic/basic nature of oxides down group
prompt: Nature of B₂O₃, the oxide of the first member of group 13?
explain: Boron is a non-metal, so B₂O₃ is acidic (it gives boric acid with water).

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acidic/basic nature of oxides down group
prompt: Which group 15 oxide is basic in nature?
explain: Bi₂O₃ is basic. As₂O₃ and Sb₂O₃ are amphoteric, and P₄O₆ is acidic.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acidic/basic nature of oxides down group
prompt: Nature of SnO₂ and PbO₂ in group 14?
explain: The heavier group 14 dioxides, SnO₂ and PbO₂, are amphoteric.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acidic/basic nature of oxides down group
prompt: Which group 14 oxide is neutral?
explain: CO is neutral and has no acidic or basic character. CO₂ and SiO₂ are acidic.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acidic/basic nature of oxides down group
prompt: Which of these nitrogen oxides is neutral?
explain: N₂O and NO are neutral. N₂O₃, NO₂ and N₂O₅ are acidic.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acidic/basic nature of oxides down group
prompt: Down group 15, the acidic character of the M₂O₃ oxides:
options: Decreases, ending in a basic oxide
explain: Metallic character rises down the group, so oxides go from acidic through amphoteric to basic.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acidic/basic nature of oxides down group
prompt: Most acidic among CO₂, SiO₂, GeO₂, SnO₂?
explain: Acidic character of group 14 dioxides decreases down the group, so CO₂ is the most acidic.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acidic/basic nature of oxides down group
prompt: Most acidic among SO₂, SeO₂, TeO₂?
explain: Acidity of the dioxides decreases down group 16, and TeO₂ is amphoteric.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acidic/basic nature of oxides down group
prompt: Nature of TeO₂?
explain: Down group 16, SO₂ and SeO₂ are acidic, while TeO₂ becomes amphoteric.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acidic/basic nature of oxides down group
prompt: Nature of NO₂, which gives HNO₂ and HNO₃ with water?
explain: NO₂ is the mixed anhydride of HNO₂ and HNO₃, so it is acidic.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acidic/basic nature of oxides down group
prompt: Nature of Ga₂O₃, the group 13 oxide below Al₂O₃?
explain: Al₂O₃ and Ga₂O₃ are amphoteric; In₂O₃ is weakly basic and Tl₂O₃ is basic.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Acidic/basic nature of oxides down group
prompt: Which oxide of group 14 is amphoteric as the +2 oxide, unlike CO₂ (acidic)?
explain: PbO is amphoteric (dissolves in acids and alkalis); SnO also amphoteric; CO is neutral, SiO is unstable.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: HF is the weakest hydrohalic acid mainly because of its
explain: The H–F bond is the strongest (≈565 kJ/mol), so ionisation is difficult; HF is the only weak hydrohalic acid.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Thermal stability order of hydrogen halides
explain: The H–X bond enthalpy decreases down the group, so HF is the most stable and HI the least.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Thermal stability order of group 14 hydrides
explain: The E–H bond weakens as the size of E increases down the group, so CH₄ is the most stable.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Order of H–E–H bond angle in group 16 hydrides
explain: Bond angle falls down the group as electronegativity falls: H₂O 104.5°, H₂S 92°, H₂Se 91°, H₂Te 90°.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which pair of H–E–H bond angles is correct for NH₃ and PH₃?
explain: The bond angle decreases down the group: NH₃ 107°, PH₃ ≈ 93.5°. Lower electronegativity of P gives more lp–bp repulsion and less bp–bp repulsion.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Conc. H₂SO₄ is reduced to SO₂ by which hydrogen halide?
options: None of HF, HCl or HBr
explain: HBr and HI are strong enough reductants to reduce conc. H₂SO₄ to SO₂ (giving Br₂ or I₂); HCl and HF are not.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which hydride ignites spontaneously in air?
explain: Higher silanes and SiH₄ are much more reactive than CH₄ because Si–H is weak and Si–O is strong; they catch fire in air.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Order of hydrogen bond strength
explain: H-bond strength increases with the electronegativity of the atom: F > O > N.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Acidic strength of second-period hydrides, in the order of increasing strength:
explain: Acidity rises across a period as the electronegativity of E increases, so the conjugate base is more stable: CH₄ < NH₃ < H₂O < HF.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Why is BF₃ a weaker Lewis acid than BCl₃?
options: F is less electronegative than Cl
Stronger pπ–pπ back donation in BF₃
B–F bond is longer than B–Cl
explain: Compact 2p orbitals of F overlap well with the empty 2p of B, reducing the electron deficiency of B.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Products of complete hydrolysis of BCl₃ with water?
explain: BCl₃ + 3H₂O → B(OH)₃ + 3HCl; B(OH)₃ is boric acid.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Hydrolysis of BF₃ gives boric acid and which other species?
explain: Initial HF formed combines with BF₃ to give H[BF₄]: 4BF₃ + 3H₂O → H₃BO₃ + 3HBF₄.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Hydrolysis of PCl₃ gives HCl and which acid?
explain: PCl₃ + 3H₂O → H₃PO₃ + 3HCl (P stays +3).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Partial hydrolysis of PCl₅ gives which compound?
explain: Limited water gives phosphoryl chloride; excess water gives H₃PO₄ + 5HCl.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Hydrolysis of BiCl₃ in water gives a white precipitate of?
explain: BiCl₃ + H₂O ⇌ BiOCl↓ + 2HCl; similarly SbCl₃ gives SbOCl.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: SF₆ is inert to hydrolysis whereas SF₄ is readily hydrolysed because SF₆…
options: has a lone pair on S
explain: SF₆ has six F shielding S with no lone pair; water cannot attack. SF₄ → SO₂ + HF.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Number of P–H bonds in hypophosphorous acid H₃PO₂
explain: H₃PO₂ has structure H₂P(O)OH: two P–H, one P–OH.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Number of P–OH bonds in pyrophosphoric acid H₄P₂O₇
explain: Each P has two OH, one P=O, joined by a P–O–P bridge; 4 P–OH.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Oxoacid of sulphur containing an S–S bond and S in +5 state is
explain: Dithionic acid H₂S₂O₆ has S–S bond; S is +5 each.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which oxoacid of sulphur has an S–O–S linkage (no peroxo)?
explain: Pyrosulphuric acid H₂S₂O₇ has an S–O–S bridge.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Oxidation state of P in hypophosphoric acid H₄P₂O₆
explain: 4 + 2x – 12 = 0 gives x = +4; it has a P–P bond.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Reducing character among H₃PO₂, H₃PO₃, H₃PO₄ is highest in
explain: P–H bonds confer reducing nature; H₃PO₂ has two and reduces Ag⁺ to Ag.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Acid strength order of halic(I) acids HOX
explain: Higher electronegativity of X stabilises the anion, so acidity falls down the group.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Basicity of hypophosphoric acid H₄P₂O₆ is
explain: It has four P–OH groups, so it is tetrabasic.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Among NH₃, PH₃, AsH₃, SbH₃, which has the highest boiling point?
explain: SbH₃ (254.6 K) exceeds NH₃ (~240 K); H-bonding in NH₃ is weaker than SbH₃'s large van der Waals forces.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which Group 13 element has an unusually low melting point (~303 K) and melts in the hand?
explain: Gallium melts at about 303 K, which is the lowest in Group 13 because of its unusual structure with Ga₂ units.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which element has the lowest boiling point (~4.2 K) of all substances?
explain: Helium has extremely weak dispersion forces, so it has the lowest boiling point (4.2 K) and boils below even H₂.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which Group 13 element has by far the highest melting point (~2453 K)?
explain: Boron has a hard covalent network of icosahedral B₁₂ units, giving a very high melting point.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Correct order of negative electron gain enthalpy (magnitude) among O, S, Se, Te is:
explain: Δ_egH: S > Se > Te > O; the compact 2p of O causes strong repulsion, so O is least negative among them except Te.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Oxygen exists as O₂ but sulphur as S₈ rings, because oxygen:
options: Has vacant d-orbitals that S lacks
Forms strong pπ–pπ double bonds, unlike S
Has a lower electronegativity than S
Has weaker O–O single bonds than S–S bonds
explain: Small O forms strong pπ–pπ O=O; large S has weak pπ–pπ overlap, so it prefers S–S single bonds in S₈.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: The only known oxoacid of fluorine is:
explain: Fluorine, being most electronegative with no d-orbitals, forms only HOF (hypofluorous acid), unlike Cl, Br, I.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Cl₂ reacts with hot concentrated NaOH to give NaCl, water and which other product?
explain: In hot conc. alkali, hypochlorite disproportionates further, so chlorate (NaClO₃) forms.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Cl₂ reacts with excess NH₃ to give NH₄Cl and which other product?
explain: With excess NH₃, N₂ and NH₄Cl form; with excess Cl₂ the product is NCl₃ instead.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: F₂ is the strongest oxidising halogen mainly due to low F–F bond enthalpy and which other factor?
options: Very high hydration enthalpy of F⁻
explain: Weak F–F bond plus highly negative hydration enthalpy of F⁻ make F₂ the strongest oxidant.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Iodine is oxidised by hot concentrated HNO₃ to which product?
explain: I₂ is oxidised to iodic acid (HIO₃, I = +5) and HNO₃ is reduced to NO₂.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which of these is an electron-precise hydride?
explain: CH₄ has exactly enough electrons for all its bonds. B₂H₆ is electron-deficient; NH₃ and H₂O are electron-rich.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Number of terminal 2c–2e B–H bonds in diborane, B₂H₆?
explain: B₂H₆ has 4 terminal 2c–2e B–H bonds and 2 bridging 3c–2e B–H–B bonds.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Conc. H₂SO₄ is reduced to which product by HI?
explain: HI is the strongest reductant among HX, so it reduces H₂SO₄ all the way to H₂S (and I₂).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: PH₃ reacts with HI to give which compound?
explain: PH₃ is a weak base and forms phosphonium iodide, PH₄I. It does not form phosphonium salts with water.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Complete hydrolysis of PCl₅ with excess water gives HCl and:
explain: Excess water converts POCl₃ fully to H₃PO₄ (P stays +5) with HCl.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Hydrolysis of SF₄ gives HF and which sulphur compound?
explain: S(+4) is retained, so SF₄ gives SO₂ and HF.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Hydrolysis of SiCl₄ gives HCl and:
explain: Si uses vacant d-orbitals for attack by water, giving Si(OH)₄ and HCl.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: In the solid state, PCl₅ exists as:
explain: Solid PCl₅ is ionic: tetrahedral cation and octahedral anion.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Fullerenes are prepared by
options: arc heating graphite in inert gas
explain: Fullerenes form when graphite is heated in an electric arc in an inert atmosphere (He/Ar); soot is extracted with benzene.
